subject: Chemistry
central_question: How does the oxygen functional group and its molecular environment determine the preparation, acidity, physical properties and reactions of alcohols, phenols and ethers?
in_scope_units: Classification and nomenclature of alcohols, phenols and ethers.
Structures and bonding of C–O and O–H functional groups.
Preparation of alcohols from alkenes, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and Grignard reagents.
Preparation of phenols from haloarenes, benzene sulphonic acid, diazonium salts and cumene.
Physical properties of alcohols and phenols, including hydrogen bonding and solubility.
Chemical reactions of alcohols and phenols, including acidity, substitution, dehydration, oxidation and electrophilic substitution.
Commercially important alcohols: methanol and ethanol.
Preparation, physical properties and chemical reactions of ethers.
banned_topics: Detailed carbonyl-compound chemistry beyond its use in preparing alcohols, which belongs to the following chapter.
Detailed haloalkane substitution mechanisms beyond Williamson ether synthesis and alcohol conversions.
Biochemical metabolism of alcohols, which is outside the chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Phenol is simply an aromatic alcohol and reacts exactly like an aliphatic alcohol.
known_pitfalls.correction: Phenol has the OH group directly attached to an sp² aromatic carbon; resonance changes its acidity and makes the aryl C–O bond resistant to ordinary substitution.

known_pitfalls.claim: Tertiary alcohols oxidise easily to ketones without carbon-chain cleavage.
known_pitfalls.correction: Tertiary alcohols lack an alpha hydrogen and resist ordinary oxidation; strong conditions may cause C–C bond cleavage.

known_pitfalls.claim: All alcohols are freely soluble in water.
known_pitfalls.correction: Solubility decreases as the hydrophobic hydrocarbon part becomes larger, despite the OH group’s hydrogen bonding.

known_pitfalls.claim: Williamson synthesis is equally suitable with tertiary alkyl halides.
known_pitfalls.correction: Tertiary halides undergo elimination with alkoxide; Williamson synthesis is best with primary alkyl halides in an SN2 reaction.

known_pitfalls.claim: Ethers cannot react because they lack an O–H bond.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are less reactive but undergo cleavage with concentrated HI or HBr and aromatic ethers undergo ring substitution.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Example 7.1 on IUPAC names.
Use NCERT Example 7.2 for alcohol preparation from reduction, hydration and a Grignard reagent.
Use NCERT Examples 7.3 and 7.4 for boiling-point and acidity orders.
Use NCERT Example 7.5 for alcohol and phenol reaction products.
Finish with NCERT Examples 7.6 and 7.7 on Williamson synthesis and ether cleavage.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 7.1 to 7.33 and cover nomenclature, preparation, physical properties, acidity, reaction mechanisms, ethers and multistep conversions.
